note: Working name. The capitals of A. W. N. Pugin, Glossary of Ecclesiastical Ornament (1844), plate 9 ('Alphabets No. 1'). Rows are listed as they appear on the plate, left to right. Where Pugin gives two forms of a letter, both are kept with neutral suffixes (.1, .2) until the defaults are chosen.

forms.M.1: uncial M: rounded, closed with a hairline
forms.T.2: uncial T: rounded, with a curl in the counter
forms.W.1: W as two interlaced V forms
forms.W.2: W as a rounded double U
forms.ornament.dots: four groups of four dots around a central dot

curl.note: the scroll terminal: a bar or stroke end that rolls into a ball, turning back toward the letter. The template is the ball and the start of its stroke only, so curls are found whatever they hang from.

font.name: Pugin Lombardic Draft
font.cap_height_px: measurements.json: summary.height.median_px (the plate's median letter height, curls included)

spacing.note: Spacing and kerning judged a pair at a time (tools/type/spacing.py), in font units over the zone from the baseline to the cap height. Side bearings are fitted so every pair of letters comes as near as it can to one target white; the pairs still off are kerned. Provisional values, to be judged on the proof page.
spacing.depth_note: each line's gap counts no further than this beyond the pair's closest approach
spacing.mean_side_bearings_note: a letter's two side bearings together, on average over the letters: lower sets tighter (the first pass set about 103)
spacing.clearance_note: no pair comes closer than this at its closest approach, so curls never touch
